text: Nebulae, vast clouds of gas and dust in space, are the birthplaces of stars. These mysterious stellar nurseries are illuminated by the light of stars already formed within them, giving birth to new ones. Through the intricate patterns of glowing gas, nebulas reveal the raw materials of the cosmos, composing dust and gas into celestial structures like stellar aggregates and even entire galaxies. As these dense regions collapse under their own gravity, gravity becomes the dominant force, causing the collapse to ignite the nuclear fusion process in the core of a newly formed star. Nebulae, therefore, are critical in the lifecycle of stars, serving as incubators for new suns to shine. Observations of nebulae, from Hubble Space Telescope snapshots to ground-based telescopic portraits, provide a window into the cosmic processes that sculpt the universe.
